description: Causal Attitude Networks (CAN) as the mechanism that generates the substrate's grounding vectors. Borsboom, Dalege, van Harreveld et al. reframed attitudes: NOT latent variables expressed in correlated indicators, but NETWORKS of causally interacting evaluations + beliefs + behavioural intentions. Each Concept is a node with state σ ∈ {-1, 0, +1} (or continuous); causally coupled to other concepts via causal_influence edges with weight J_ij; driven by external field h_i (current evidence + object salience); at effective inverse temperature β (= attention level on that frame). Network Hamiltonian H = -ΣJ_ij σ_i σ_j - Σh_i σ_i. Equilibrium distribution P(σ) ∝ exp(-βH) (Boltzmann). The 'grounding vector' from grounding_theory is the marginal expectation ⟨σ⟩ at equilibrium — DERIVED, not primitive. Stability = local energy minimum. Attitude strength = network connectivity. Ambivalence = spin-glass frustration. Polarisation = phase transition at low T. Multiple inconsistent views = multistable network with distinct basins. The substrate's existing features map cleanly: babble = MCMC sampling, predicate churn = bistability with thermal flips, conviction = J × β, coherence = -H/N, curiosity = expected info gain about σ.
category_inheritance: genlMt → compiler_theory + philosophy + mathematics + grounding_theory. CAN gives a generative mechanism for grounding_theory's vector. Mathematics provides Ising machinery (statistical mechanics on graphs, MCMC, free energy). Philosophy provides Axiom 0 (frame-relativity → network state lives in a frame; multiple frames = multiple Hamiltonians coexisting).

concepts.name: CAN_Borsboom_Dalege
concepts.definition: Causal Attitude Network model. Borsboom (psychometrics), Dalege + van Harreveld (social psychology). 2016 'Toward a formalized account of attitudes' (Psych Review).
concepts.why: Foundation. Reframed attitudes after decades of latent-variable orthodoxy. Borsboom + Cramer earlier did same for psychopathology (symptom networks).

concepts.name: attitudes_not_latent_variables
concepts.definition: Classical view: latent construct (the attitude) causes its observable indicators (correlated responses). CAN view: NO latent construct — the network IS the attitude.
concepts.why: Foundation distinction. Latent-variable thinking treats observed pattern as effect; CAN treats it as constitutive. Different ontology, different statistics.

concepts.name: evaluations_beliefs_behaviours_as_nodes
concepts.definition: Each node = one specific evaluation ('this is good'), belief ('this causes X'), or behavioural intention ('I would do Y'). Many per attitude object.
concepts.why: Granularity. Attitude toward 'climate change' = many nodes: 'CO2 traps heat', 'humans cause warming', 'will harm grandchildren', 'should reduce emissions'. Each its own node.

concepts.name: node_state_sigma
concepts.definition: σ_i = state of node i. Binary (±1, agree/disagree), trinary (-1, 0, +1), or continuous.
concepts.why: Foundation Ising variable. Marginal expectation ⟨σ_i⟩ ∈ [-1, +1] is the dimension's contribution to grounding vector. Substrate: each Concept gains state attr.

concepts.name: coupling_J_ij
concepts.definition: J_ij = causal influence strength between nodes i and j. Positive: mutual reinforcement. Negative: mutual inhibition. Asymmetric possible (directed).
concepts.why: Foundation. J encodes 'believing this makes me more (or less) likely to believe that'. Strong attitudes = high |J| densely. Substrate: refers_to edges become causal_influence edges with J.

concepts.name: external_field_h_i
concepts.definition: h_i = external bias on node i. Encodes evidence, object salience, prior. Positive h: world pushes node toward +1.
concepts.why: How world enters. Sensory evidence on perceptual node; testimonial evidence from others; structural pressure from Mt commitments. Substrate: per-Concept external_field attr.

concepts.name: inverse_temperature_beta
concepts.definition: β = 1/T. High β (low T) = states crystallise into definite values. Low β (high T) = states diffuse + uncertain. β scales BOTH J + h.
concepts.why: Foundation. CAN connects β to attention: attention to attitude object → effective β rises → polarisation. Substrate: per-Mt temperature; attended frames have higher β.

concepts.name: Hamiltonian_H
concepts.definition: H(σ) = -Σ_{i<j} J_ij σ_i σ_j - Σ_i h_i σ_i. Energy of configuration σ.
concepts.why: Foundation. Lower H = more stable. Equilibrium states minimise H locally. Substrate operations: compute H, find local minima, identify basins.

concepts.name: Boltzmann_distribution
concepts.definition: P(σ) = exp(-βH(σ)) / Z. Z = partition function = Σ_σ exp(-βH).
concepts.why: Foundation. Equilibrium distribution over network states. High β: distribution sharp on minima. Low β: spread. Substrate samples via MCMC.

concepts.name: marginal_expectation_is_grounding
concepts.definition: ⟨σ_i⟩ = Σ_σ σ_i P(σ). The marginal expectation at equilibrium. This IS the i-th component of the grounding vector.
concepts.why: Bridge to grounding_theory. The 'grounding vector' isn't primitive — it's the network's equilibrium marginal. CAN provides the generative model the vector was missing.

concepts.name: Metropolis_Hastings_update
concepts.definition: Propose σ_i → σ_i'. Accept with probability min(1, exp(-βΔH)). Generates Boltzmann samples.
concepts.why: Standard MCMC. Substrate uses to sample equilibrium. Each step is local; many steps → equilibrium. Fast for sparse networks.

concepts.name: Glauber_dynamics
concepts.definition: Sequentially update each node σ_i to ±1 with probabilities ∝ exp(-βE_i(±1)). Stochastic per-node update.
concepts.why: Alternative to Metropolis. Detailed balance. Models gradual belief revision: one node at a time updates based on its local field (couplings + external).

concepts.name: mean_field_approximation
concepts.definition: Replace neighbours' states with their averages. Self-consistent equation: ⟨σ_i⟩ = tanh(β(Σ_j J_ij ⟨σ_j⟩ + h_i)).
concepts.why: Fast deterministic approximation. Substrate uses for quick estimates of marginals without full MCMC. Exact for dense networks; approximate for sparse.

concepts.name: stability_local_minimum
concepts.definition: State σ* is locally stable if H(σ*) ≤ H(σ) for all σ differing in one node. Bistability + multistability possible.
concepts.why: Why some beliefs resist revision. Substrate's 'stability' aspect emerges: high stability = deep local minimum. Predicate churn = sitting at saddle between minima.

concepts.name: attitude_strength_is_connectivity
concepts.definition: Strong attitude = high network connectivity (many nodes, high |J|). Resists external perturbation.
concepts.why: Foundation CAN result. Strong attitudes hard to change because many constituents reinforce each other. Substrate: 'conviction' aspect = network density measure.

concepts.name: ambivalence_spin_glass_frustration
concepts.definition: Network has frustrated couplings: no σ satisfies all J_ij. Multiple low-but-not-lowest minima. High residual energy.
concepts.why: Mechanism for ambivalence + cognitive dissonance. NOT just 'conflicting opinions' — specific spin-glass structure. Substrate detects via energy gap + multistability.

concepts.name: polarisation_phase_transition
concepts.definition: At critical β_c, network undergoes phase transition: symmetric → broken-symmetry (definite states). Sharper for stronger couplings.
concepts.why: Foundation. Attention crosses β_c → opinions snap into place. Below: ambivalent. Critical phenomena explain polarisation dynamics.

concepts.name: attention_modulates_beta
concepts.definition: Dalege et al.: attention to attitude object increases effective β. Engaged = polarised; uninterested = diffuse.
concepts.why: Foundation CAN result. Explains: priming + thinking-about-it leads to extreme views. Substrate: focused-on Mts have high effective β.

concepts.name: multiple_basins_multiple_views
concepts.definition: Network with multiple low-energy basins = multistable. State can sit in any. Each basin = coherent set of beliefs (e.g. folk physics OR scientific physics).
concepts.why: Mechanism for grounding_theory's 'multiple inconsistent views'. Not orthogonal vector components — distinct attractors in same network. Thermal noise / new evidence flips between.

concepts.name: evidence_shifts_field
concepts.definition: New evidence at node i changes h_i. Field shift drives state update via dynamics. Strong evidence dominates; weak gets damped by network.
concepts.why: Mechanism of belief revision. h alone doesn't fix σ; the network's J pull back if internally incoherent. Substrate models: how does evidence flow through network?

concepts.name: basin_hopping_belief_revision
concepts.definition: Sufficient field change or thermal fluctuation can flip network from one basin to another. Sudden conversion, gestalt switch.
concepts.why: Mechanism for paradigm shift, Kuhnian conversion. Not gradual move — discrete basin transition. Substrate observes: sudden coherence shifts vs gradual drift.

concepts.name: free_energy_F
concepts.definition: F = -T log Z. At equilibrium, system minimises free energy F = ⟨H⟩ - TS. Balances energy + entropy.
concepts.why: Foundation. Free energy = effective potential. Substrate's 'coherence' aspect ≈ -F/N (negative free energy density). Low F = coherent + stable.

concepts.name: coupling_learning_Hebbian
concepts.definition: J_ij learned over time: J_ij ← J_ij + η σ_i σ_j (Hebbian). Co-activated nodes become coupled.
concepts.why: Mechanism for attitude formation. 'Fire together, wire together' for beliefs. Substrate: how do J_ij get set? Learned from co-occurrence of states.

concepts.name: field_calibration_from_world
concepts.definition: h_i set by accumulated evidence: h_i = (positive evidence count) - (negative evidence count), weighted by reliability.
concepts.why: Mechanism for how world enters. Sensor evidence on perceptual nodes, testimony on others. Substrate's existing 'observation' becomes field update.

concepts.name: info_gain_drives_curiosity
concepts.definition: Curiosity = expected reduction in entropy of σ distribution. Probe nodes where high uncertainty (state near 0, ambivalent).
concepts.why: Substrate's curiosity drive formalised. Bayesian: minimise expected posterior entropy. Practical: investigate ambivalent (frustrated) parts of network.

concepts.name: babble_is_MCMC_sampling
concepts.definition: Babble loop = thermal stochastic sampling of network state. Each cycle = one (or many) Metropolis updates. Estimates marginals.

b.value: thermal stochastic sampling of network state

concepts.why: Substrate's existing babble loop maps directly. Existing phonology divergence work uses same: sample → estimate marginal → impasse-or-not.

concepts.name: predicate_churn_is_bistability
concepts.definition: Substrate's 'predicate churn' Impasse = network sitting at saddle between two basins, thermally flipping. Not noise — specific dynamics.
concepts.why: Mechanism. Currently substrate detects predicate churn as 'still changing'. CAN: it's bistability + thermal noise. Resolution: more evidence + lower T (more attention).

concepts.name: conviction_is_J_times_beta
concepts.definition: Effective conviction at node i ≈ Σ_j |J_ij| × β. High coupling × high attention = unshakeable.
concepts.why: Substrate's 'conviction' aspect formalised. Not just magnitude — product of network embeddedness + attentional engagement.

concepts.name: coherence_is_negative_free_energy
concepts.definition: Coherence(network) ∝ -F/N = (energy term + entropy term)/N. Low F = mutually-supporting beliefs at low temperature.
concepts.why: Substrate's 'coherence' aspect formalised. Not a separate measure — emergent from H + temperature. Free energy = system's effective potential.

concepts.name: Mt_is_subnetwork_with_signature_couplings
concepts.definition: A Microtheory = a subset of nodes + characteristic coupling pattern. The Mt's 'commitments' are constraints encoded in its J.
concepts.why: Mapping Mts to CAN. Folk_physics Mt = nodes for everyday physical beliefs + couplings supporting folk-coherent assignments. Scientific_physics Mt = same nodes, different J.

concepts.name: multiple_Mts_multiple_Hamiltonians
concepts.definition: Different Mts contribute different J_ij to same nodes. Total Hamiltonian = Σ_Mt H_Mt. Frame-relativity = different J in different frames.
concepts.why: Bridge to grounding_theory. Axiom 0's frame-relativity becomes: there are multiple Hamiltonians coexisting on the same node set. Each Mt's grounding marginal = ⟨σ⟩ under THAT Mt's H.

concepts.name: frame_switch_changes_active_Hamiltonian
concepts.definition: Switching attention to a different Mt switches the active Hamiltonian. Network re-equilibrates. Same nodes, different basins, different marginals.
concepts.why: How substrate moves between frames. Per-frame attention β + Mt-specific couplings = different equilibria. Substrate query: 'is X grounded in Mt_y?' = marginal under H_{Mt_y}.

concepts.name: wrongness_is_distance_to_target_marginal
concepts.definition: Distance from current ⟨σ⟩ to target ⟨σ⟩* under target H*. With direction (which nodes off) + magnitude.
concepts.why: Refines grounding_theory's wrongness. Not arbitrary target vector — target is itself an equilibrium of a target H. 'How wrong' = how far from target attractor.

concepts.name: diagnostic_per_node_deviation
concepts.definition: (⟨σ_i⟩ - ⟨σ_i⟩*) per node. Which beliefs deviate from target. Can be due to wrong h, wrong J, or insufficient relaxation.
concepts.why: Targeted self-correction. Substrate can identify: 'belief X is the off-node; trace its couplings + field for source'. Vector grounding's diagnosis gains mechanism.

concepts.name: network_size_grows_with_learning
concepts.definition: New beliefs = new nodes. New couplings learned via Hebbian updates as beliefs co-activate. Network grows with experience.
concepts.why: Mechanism for substrate's growth. Concepts added; coupled to existing via Hebbian as they co-occur. Network thickens. Strength of attitudes accumulates structurally.

concepts.name: Ising_model_history
concepts.definition: Ising 1925 (ferromagnetism). Decades of physics. Adopted: epilepsy (Hopfield), neural networks (Hopfield + Boltzmann machines), opinion dynamics, psychometric networks.
concepts.why: Foundation is well-developed. CAN inherits all the Ising machinery. Substrate not inventing — connecting to a deep mathematical lineage.

concepts.name: Hopfield_network_associative_memory
concepts.definition: Hopfield 1982: Ising network with learned couplings stores patterns as attractors. Retrieval = relaxation to nearest attractor.
concepts.why: Direct precedent. Belief patterns as attractors. Substrate's 'recognition' = network relaxation to closest stored pattern. Familiar territory.

concepts.name: Boltzmann_machine_learning
concepts.definition: Hinton + Sejnowski 1985: stochastic Ising with hidden units. Learns to model distributions via contrastive divergence.
concepts.why: Direct precedent for learning the J. RBMs etc. Substrate borrows learning machinery: contrastive divergence on observed states updates J.

concepts.name: psychopathology_network_Cramer_Borsboom
concepts.definition: Cramer + Borsboom: depression NOT a latent disease causing symptoms; depression IS the network of causally interacting symptoms.
concepts.why: Same methodological move as CAN, applied to clinical. Network analysis of symptom-symptom edges. Substrate's grounding parallels: not a latent property but the network.

concepts.name: concept_state_attr_substrate
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Concept gains state σ ∈ [-1, +1] attribute. Initialised to 0; updated by dynamics.
concepts.why: Concrete schema change. Backwards compatible: legacy code that doesn't read state sees normal Concept. Vector-aware code computes ⟨σ⟩ from state + couplings.

concepts.name: causal_influence_edge_type
concepts.definition: Architecturally: new edge type causal_influence with weight J (signed). Replaces refers_to for grounding purposes.
concepts.why: Concrete schema. refers_to was binary; causal_influence is signed-weighted. J_ij = +0.7 (strong positive coupling), -0.4 (weak inhibition).

concepts.name: external_field_attr_substrate
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Concept gains external_field h ∈ R attribute. Updated when world produces evidence on that node.
concepts.why: Concrete schema. World adapters update h; dynamics update σ in response. Field-state separation cleanly separates world from network.

concepts.name: Mt_temperature_attr
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Microtheory gains β attribute (effective inverse temperature). Attention = high β; passive = low β.
concepts.why: Concrete schema. Per-Mt attention level. Active reasoning in physics Mt: β high → equilibration sharp. Idle: β low → diffuse.

concepts.name: dynamics_module_metropolis_glauber
concepts.definition: Architecturally: dynamics module supporting Metropolis, Glauber, mean-field. Operates on Concept states + causal_influence edges.
concepts.why: Concrete code. Each Mt's reflexes can invoke updates. Babble loop = repeated MH steps. Convergence detection via free energy.

concepts.name: Impasse_becomes_network_diagnosis
concepts.definition: Architecturally: Impasses gain network-state diagnostics. Predicate churn = bistability + θ flipping rate. Frustration = energy gap. Ambivalence = high entropy.
concepts.why: Concrete schema. Existing Impasses extended with network observables. Already vector-shaped after grounding_theory; now CAN-grounded interpretation.

concepts.name: migration_from_binary_to_CAN
concepts.definition: Architecturally: existing refers_to edges → causal_influence with J=+1 (strong positive). Existing Unknowns → Concept with field=0, decoupled.
concepts.why: Concrete migration path. Legacy graph becomes CAN graph with trivial structure. Subsequent edits set proper J, h. Substrate becomes CAN-native incrementally.

concepts.name: frequentist_vs_thermal_sampling
concepts.definition: Frequentist statistics: repeated trials yield distributions. CAN: thermal fluctuations of network yield distributions. Same math, different interpretation.
concepts.why: Substrate doesn't run trials — it runs MCMC on its own network. Stationary distribution = belief distribution. Bayesian by construction.

concepts.name: CAN_vs_predictive_processing
concepts.definition: Predictive processing: brain minimises prediction error via hierarchical generative model. CAN: minimises free energy via network dynamics. Closely related; CAN simpler + explicit.
concepts.why: Substrate's design close to PP framework. CAN is concrete + amenable to graph-resident expression. Bridges to active inference literature.

concepts.name: CAN_vs_Bayesian_network
concepts.definition: Bayesian network: directed acyclic, conditional probabilities. CAN: undirected (or asymmetric), couplings. Bayesian computes posteriors via inference; CAN via thermal equilibrium.
concepts.why: Different formalism, related questions. CAN handles cycles + bidirectional influence natively. Bayes-net inference is special case of CAN at zero temperature.

rules.name: attitudes_are_networks_not_latents
then: it should be modelled as network, not latent variable
rules.why: Borsboom + Dalege foundational shift. Network treats indicators as constitutive + causally interacting. Latent treats them as effects of unobserved cause. Different ontology, different stats, different interventions.

rules.name: grounding_vector_is_equilibrium_marginal
then: answer is marginal ⟨σ⟩ at equilibrium under applicable Hamiltonian
rules.why: Refines grounding_theory. Vector isn't primitive; it's derived from network dynamics. Generative mechanism. The vector has a story for how it got that way.

rules.name: strong_attitudes_are_densely_coupled
then: underlying network has high connectivity + strong J
rules.why: Foundation CAN result. Belief perseverance has mechanism: network's many couplings mutually support assignment. Single-node perturbation insufficient.

rules.name: attention_increases_polarisation
if: attention to attitude object increases (β rises)
then: network polarises further toward existing basin
rules.why: Foundation CAN result. Engagement crystallises. Explains: thinking about politics makes views stronger, not more nuanced. Critical phenomena.

rules.name: ambivalence_is_frustration_not_indecision
then: ambivalence + high energy + no clean assignment
rules.why: Mechanism vs description. Not 'undecided' — specific spin-glass structure. Detectable via energy gap. Different from low conviction (low coupling).

rules.name: multiple_inconsistent_views_are_multistable_basins
then: network has multiple stable basins, state can sit in either
rules.why: Refines grounding_theory's 'multiple inconsistent views'. Not orthogonal vector components — distinct attractors. Mechanism for paradigm switch (basin hop).

rules.name: babble_loop_is_thermal_sampling
then: it's MCMC on its own network
rules.why: Reframes existing mechanism. Substrate babble = Metropolis chain. Cycles → marginals → grounding. The mechanism that was lurking is now named.

rules.name: predicate_churn_is_bistable_thermal_flipping
then: network is bistable + temperature too high
rules.why: Mechanism for substrate's existing Impasse. Resolution: more evidence (raise effective h) OR more attention (raise β) → freeze into one basin.

rules.name: Hebbian_learning_updates_J
rules.why: Mechanism for coupling formation. Substrate's experience: co-occurring states strengthen mutual influence. Network grows through use.

rules.name: Mt_relativity_is_multiple_Hamiltonians
if: concept grounded differently in different Mts
then: each Mt contributes its own H + marginal
rules.why: Axiom 0 made concrete. Different Mts = different J on (possibly same) nodes. Each Mt's H has its own equilibrium. Frame switch = active Hamiltonian switch.

rules.name: wrongness_is_distance_to_target_equilibrium
then: distance is from current ⟨σ⟩ to target H*'s equilibrium ⟨σ⟩*
rules.why: Refines grounding_theory wrongness. Not arbitrary target — target is itself an attractor of some target H. Direction + magnitude + mechanism for correction.

rules.name: coherence_is_negative_free_energy_density
rules.why: Foundation. Low F = nodes mutually supporting + appropriately uncertain. Substrate's 'coherence' aspect grounded in statistical mechanics.

rules.name: evidence_changes_field_then_relaxation
rules.why: Mechanism for belief revision. Evidence doesn't directly set state — it changes field; field changes drive dynamics; network finds new equilibrium. Possibly basin-hops.

rules.name: curiosity_targets_ambivalent_nodes
then: nodes with high state uncertainty (near 0) are highest info gain
rules.why: Curiosity drive formalised. Ambivalent nodes (no clean basin yet) provide most info. Substrate's existing 'investigate impasse' aligns.
rules.comment: WIRED 2026-08-13 (CAN_BELIEF_QUANTIZATION_RESULTS.md) -- the RECOGNIZE half of this rule, using ONLY existing DSL Terms (Attr/Abs/Lt/Not/Eq), no new Rust. Presupposes a Concept's `state` attr already reflects the current equilibrium (mt_relax_to_marginal or mt_mean_field_marginal + a write-back has already run this tick -- this rule does not itself compute the mean field, it only classifies an ALREADY-COMPUTED state, exactly as node_local_frustration's own docstring requires of its caller). Flags any has_concept member whose |state| < 0.05 as is_ambivalent=1, idempotent (guarded so it does not refire once flagged). A Concept with no `state` attr at all defaults (via the DSL Attr term's Value::None -> as_f64() = 0.0 fallback) to counting as ambivalent too -- consistent with this project's own documented 'Unknown = zero vector' convention (can_ops.rs distance_to_target docstring), not a bug. This is deliberately the RECOGNIZE half only: the UPDATE/RELAX half (mean-field relaxation, Hebbian J update, energy/frustration) has NO DSL Term surface at all today (can_ops.rs is reachable only via direct PyO3 Python calls, never from inside a Rule's own effects) -- see CAN_BELIEF_QUANTIZATION_RESULTS.md Q4 for why the other 14 rules stay undecided rather than force-wired.

rules.name: CAN_is_substrate_grounding_mechanism
rules.why: Substrate's design position. Grounding vectors are observables of underlying network. Vectors without networks underneath are unmechanism'd. CAN supplies what was missing.
